abstract_theorem.setup: Let h>=0 be self-adjoint with exp(-t h) trace class for every t>0. Fix a,b>=0, put B=a h+b I, and let the symmetric form perturbation have the Kato factorization V=B^(1/2) C B^(1/2) with C=C* and ||C||<=1. For beta>0 put A_beta=Tr[B^(1/2)exp(-beta h/2)] and K_beta(s)=exp[-(beta-s)h]V exp(-s h), 0<s<beta.
abstract_theorem.half_interval_bound: For 0<s<=beta/2, ||K_beta(s)||_1<=A_beta[sqrt(b)+sqrt(a/(2 e s))]. For beta/2<=s<beta, ||K_beta(s)||_1<=A_beta[sqrt(b)+sqrt(a/(2 e (beta-s)))]. Both bounds follow by using one Gibbs-dressed B^(1/2) factor in trace norm and the other in operator norm.
abstract_theorem.integrability: The two half-interval majorants are integrable and give integral_0^beta ||K_beta(s)||_1 ds<=A_beta[beta sqrt(b)+2 sqrt(a beta/e)]. Thus the first Duhamel operator coefficient exists as an S1-valued Bochner integral without the symmetric Holder-majorant premise used in R-167 v3.6.
abstract_theorem.ritz_passage: If Pi_M are increasing finite-rank spectral projections of h with Pi_M->I strongly, then K_(beta,M)(s)=Pi_M K_beta(s) Pi_M converges pointwise in trace norm and in L1((0,beta);S1). Consequently the compressed first Duhamel operator integrals converge in trace norm to the full-oscillator coefficient.
abstract_theorem.trace_identity: For every 0<s<beta, trace cyclicity gives Tr K_beta(s)=Tr[C B exp(-beta h)], hence Tr integral_0^beta K_beta(s) ds=beta Tr[C B exp(-beta h)].
abstract_theorem.heat_trace_bound: Writing Z_h(t)=Tr exp(-t h), A_beta<=sqrt(a)sqrt(2/(e beta)) Z_h(beta/4)+sqrt(b)Z_h(beta/2).
abstract_theorem.boundary: This is an exact first-Duhamel and spectral-Ritz-removal theorem. It does not control higher Duhamel coefficients, time-simplex combinatorics, contour entropy or DFFR transition norms.

q3_application.setup: For one exact Q3 reference edge at fixed N, the inherited relative-form estimate has -B_(e,N)<=V_(e,N)<=B_(e,N) with B_(e,N)=alpha_N h^0_(e,N)+beta_N I. The confining edge reference h^0_(e,N) has compact resolvent and finite Gibbs trace.
q3_application.conclusion: For every fixed N and physical beta>0, the full-oscillator first Duhamel edge coefficient is trace class and is the trace-norm limit of its spectral Ritz compressions. No extra short-time L1 premise is needed.
q3_application.explicit_majorant: Using Z_(0,e,N)(t)<=Z_(k_N)(t/6)^2, A_(beta,e,N)<=sqrt(alpha_N)sqrt(2/(e beta))Z_(k_N)(beta/24)^2+sqrt(beta_N)Z_(k_N)(beta/12)^2. The theorem is dimension-free in the cutoff M for each fixed N,beta.
q3_application.uniformity_boundary: No N-uniform assertion follows unless uniform heat-trace and relative-form inputs are proved separately. This application is not a DFFR contour entry theorem.

relation_to_v3_6.repair: R-167 v3.6 correctly showed that the symmetric Schatten-Holder majorant g_beta(s)=sqrt(F_B(2s)F_B(2(beta-s))) need not be integrable. R-167 v3.7 uses a different one-sided trace-class/operator-norm factorization on the two half intervals and proves the actual first coefficient is integrable for affine B=a h+b I.
relation_to_v3_6.history: The v3.6 negative remains immutable and valid: it rejects automatic integrability of that symmetric majorant, not existence of a sharper majorant or of the coefficient itself.
